elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 sets notice at "at least ninety (90) days' written notice", which exceeds the 30-day preferred anchor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation appears anywhere in the rendered text; 11.1 imposes payments on Customer only and says nothing about return of prepaid fees, let alone on a pro-rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Rendered 10.2 now reads "M&I may withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services), effective only at the end of the Term" — the effective date is expressly tied to term end, so no mid-term convenience exit remains. The retained immediate right is triggered only by "final regulatory, legislative, or judicial" action, which is not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — inside the 60–90 day band and not exceeding it.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: the Termination for Convenience Fee is set "in an amount that, together with all other amounts payable by Customer under this Section 11.1, does not exceed three (3) months' fees". Because the cap expressly aggregates "all other amounts payable ... under this Section 11.1", the retained "In addition to the foregoing" unamortized Conversion costs, Expenses and disposition costs fall inside the ceiling. The retained carve-out from Section 13.4 concerns the general liability cap and does not disturb the three-month ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Rendered 10.2 deletes "at any time" and adds "effective only at the end of the Term", tying the effective date of M&I's withdrawal of non-Core Services to term end.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Already met in the original and preserved: 10.2 requires "ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: notice cut from one year to 90 days (in band), an aggregate three-month cap imposed on all Section 11.1 termination amounts, M&I's non-Core withdrawal made effective only at the end of the Term, and the pre-existing 90-day M&I notice retained.

Preferred is not reached on two elements: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is added. If the drafter wants preferred, insert "M&I shall refund any prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis for the period after the Effective Date of Termination" and reduce the notice to thirty (30) days.

Minimality holds: the only edits are the notice figure, the fee-cap formulation, and the timing anchor in 10.2. Deletion of "at any time" in 10.2 is necessary to avoid a retained sentence contradicting the new end-of-Term anchor; the 50/50 payment schedule, the Event of Default and Section 11.3 carve-outs, the Expenses language and the Section 13.4 carve-out are all preserved.

Intent preserved: no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence; the 50/50 instalment mechanic still functions under a 90-day notice window (first 50% within 30 days of notice, balance 30 days before the Effective Date of Termination).

Optional tightening (not a defect): because the ceiling is worded as a constraint on the Fee's amount "together with" other Section 11.1 amounts, consider recasting it as a standalone aggregate cap — "in no event shall the aggregate of all amounts payable by Customer under this Section 11.1 exceed three (3) months' fees" — to remove any argument that the "In addition to the foregoing" costs sit outside the cap.
Also confirm which fee base "three (3) months' fees" refers to (e.g. the average monthly fees for the three months preceding notice) so the cap does not depend on an undefined measure in a dispute.
